subject: Career
title: Total Compensation vs. Base Salary
description: Learn Total Compensation vs. Base Salary in one minute.

hook.text: Two offers: $120K base vs. $110K base with $30K bonus and equity. Which pays more?

buildup.text: Total compensation includes base, bonus, equity, benefits, retirement match, and perks.

discovery.text: Focusing only on base salary is like judging a house by the front door.

twist.text: Equity can be worth millions or nothing. Understand vesting schedules and strike prices.

climax.text: Calculate your total comp number before comparing offers. Apples to apples.

punchline.text: Base salary is the headline. Total comp is the story.

quiz.question: What does total compensation include beyond base salary?

details.summary: Many candidates fixate on base salary and overlook how bonuses, equity, benefits, and perks together form total compensation. This narrow focus can lead to rejecting superior overall packages or accepting roles where base pay masks low total value.
details.whyItMatters: Two offers with the same base salary can differ by tens of thousands when total compensation is compared. Understanding the full picture leads to more informed career decisions.
takeaways: Two identical base salaries can hide very different total comp
Equity and bonuses often differentiate competitive offers
Always request the full compensation summary before deciding

faq.question: How should I compare two job offers with different compensation structures?
faq.answer: Annualize every component into a single total compensation figure. Weight liquid cash components higher than illiquid ones like startup equity. Then factor in lifestyle variables like commute cost and PTO days.

faq.question: Is a higher base salary always better than larger equity?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Equity at a growing company can outpace base salary gains significantly. However, equity carries risk. If you need predictable income, prioritize base salary; if you can absorb risk, equity may offer more upside.
